8 : Appendix

This section contains supplementary information for the TI Cybershield Toolkit.

9.1 Glossary

HS-FS

High Security - Field Secure. Initial security state of devices where secure boot is not enforced for customer code.

HS-KP

High Security - Key Provisioned. State after key provisioning where customer keys are programmed and secure boot is enforced with customer keys.

HS-SE

High Security - Security Enabled. Final security state where the device is fully secured with customer keys and code.

SMPK

Secondary Manufacturer Public Key. Customer-owned key used for image authentication. Abbreviated SMPK.

SMEK

Secondary Manufacturer Encryption Key. Customer-owned key used for image decryption. Abbreviated SMEK.

BMPK

Backup Secondary Manufacturer Public Key. Optional customer-owned backup key for image authentication.

BMEK

Backup Secondary Manufacturer Encryption Key. Optional customer-owned backup key for image decryption.

TI FEK

Texas Instruments Field Encryption Key. TI-owned public key embedded in TI’s HSM firmware binary, used to encrypt sensitive information (RNG AES key) in provisioning certificates. Customers do not generate this key — it is fixed per device family and provided by TI.

HSM

Hardware Security Module. Dedicated hardware device for secure key storage and cryptographic operations.

PKCS#11

Public Key Cryptography Standards #11. API for cryptographic token interface.

OTP

One-Time Programmable. Memory that can be programmed only once.

CCS

Code Composer Studio. TI’s integrated development environment.

ROM Boot Mode

Initial boot mode where the device executes code from internal ROM.

UART Boot Mode

Boot mode where the device can receive code over a serial connection.

JTAG

Joint Test Action Group. Industry standard for hardware debugging.

XDS

eXtended Debug Support. TI’s debug probe technology.

Note

In TI’s device security architecture, “Manufacturer” keys are TI-owned keys (e.g., TI FEK). “Secondary Manufacturer” keys (SMPK/SMEK and their backups BMPK/BMEK) are customer-owned keys provisioned via this tool.

9.2 Error Code Reference

This section provides a reference for common error codes encountered during provisioning.

9.2.1 General Error Codes

Error Code

Description

Possible Solutions

0x00000000

Success

N/A (operation completed successfully)

0x80000001

Generic Error

Check logs for more specific information

0x80000002

Communication Error

Check physical connections and retry

0x80000003

Timeout Error

Verify device is powered and responsive

0x80000004

Authentication Error

Check certificate integrity and signature

0x80000005

Permission Error

Verify device state supports the requested operation

9.2.2 OTP Programming Error Codes

Error Code

Description

Possible Solutions

0x90000001

Field Already Programmed

Field is locked; cannot be modified

0x90000002

Invalid Field ID

Check certificate field configuration

0x90000003

Field Write Error

Hardware issue or power interruption during write

0x90000004

Field Verification Error

Written value does not match expected value

0x90000005

Field Access Error

Current device state prohibits access

9.2.3 Code Provisioning Error Codes

Error Code

Description

Possible Solutions

0xA0000001

Image Authentication Failed

Check image signature and key validity

0xA0000002

Image Decryption Failed

Verify encryption key and algorithm

0xA0000003

Flash Write Error

Check flash memory health and power stability

0xA0000004

Flash Verify Error

Written data does not match expected data

0xA0000005

Invalid Image Format

Check binary format and header

9.3 Certificate Format

9.3.1 Certificate Structure

The TI Cybershield Toolkit generates X.509 certificates with the following structure:

Certificate
├── Version
├── Serial Number
├── Signature Algorithm
├── Issuer
├── Validity Period
├── Subject
├── Subject Public Key Info
├── X.509 Extensions
│   ├── TI_Field_1 (Encrypted with TI FEK)
│   ├── TI_Field_2 (Encrypted with TI FEK)
│   ├── ...
│   └── TI_Field_N (Encrypted with TI FEK)
└── Certificate Signature

9.3.2 Certificate Fields

The certificate includes the following key fields:

  • SMPK: Secondary Manufacturer Public Key for image authentication

  • SMEK: Secondary Manufacturer Encryption Key for image decryption

  • BMPK: Backup Secondary Manufacturer Public Key (optional)

  • BMEK: Backup Secondary Manufacturer Encryption Key (optional)

  • KEY_COUNT: Number of key sets (1 or 2)

  • KEY_REVISION: Active key revision (1 or 2)

  • SWREV fields: Software revision values

  • MSV: Model Specific Value (customer-specific)

9.4 Security Recommendations

9.4.1 Key Management

  • Use strong passwords (12+ characters, mixed case, symbols) for key protection

  • Store keys in a secure, controlled environment

  • Consider using an HSM for production key operations

  • Maintain separate key sets for development and production

  • Implement a key rotation strategy for long-term product security

9.4.2 Production Environment

  • Establish a secure provisioning area with limited access

  • Use dedicated provisioning hardware that is physically secured

  • Implement procedural controls for handling security materials

  • Train personnel on security procedures and best practices

  • Maintain detailed logs of all provisioning activities

9.4.3 Post-Provisioning Verification

  • Verify device state after provisioning

  • Perform security validation tests on provisioned devices

  • Document device provisioning status and security configurations

  • Implement secure methods for tracking provisioned devices
